content: Infants under the age of 12 months have been associated with adverse outcomes related to the use of cough and cold medications. Medical examiners or coroners have determined these medications to be the underlying cause of death in certain cases. These findings emphasize the importance of clinicians exercising caution when prescribing, and caregivers being vigilant when administering, cough and cold medications to children under the age of 2 years. For further information, visit the FDA website. Codeine is commonly prescribed, often in combination with other medications, to suppress coughing. It is also used to alleviate mild to moderate pain. In some cases, it may be prescribed for other purposes; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Codeine is available as a standalone medication or in combination with other drugs, and it comes in tablet, capsule, and liquid forms for oral administration. It is typically taken every 4 to 6 hours as needed. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take codeine exactly as directed. Be aware that codeine has the potential to be habit-forming. Do not take larger doses, take it more frequently, or use it for a longer duration than prescribed by your doctor. If you are using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before measuring your dose. Before taking codeine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to codeine or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially other pain relievers, antidepressants, medications for cough, cold, or allergies, sedatives, sleeping pills, tranquilizers, and vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have a history of liver, kidney, or lung disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking codeine, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking codeine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how codeine affects you. Additionally, alcohol can enhance the drowsiness caused by this medication. If you forget to take a dose of codeine, and your doctor has instructed you to take it regularly, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Codeine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: dizziness, lightheadedness, drowsiness, upset stomach, vomiting, constipation, stomach pain, rash, or difficulty urinating. If you experience severe side effects such as difficulty breathing or mood changes, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects should be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with anyone else. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist.
